title: County of Boulogne
capsule: The County of Boulogne was a strategically vital Channel lordship, controlling the principal crossing point between England and France. The period 1188–1260 saw it pass through dramatic successions: Count Renaud de Dammartin allied with the Holy Roman Empire against Philip II of France and was captured at Bouvines in 1214, dying in imprisonment. The county passed to his daughter Matilda II, who married Philip Hurepel (son of Philip II) and later Afonso of Portugal, who became Afonso III of Portugal in 1248 and renounced his Boulogne title. Matilda's death around 1260 without surviving heirs effectively ended the direct comital line and opened a prolonged succession dispute.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's territory is reasonably well attested from feudal records and French royal charters; the core area around Boulogne is clear, though subordinate dependencies fluctuated with the political fortunes of the ruling line.
